items.rationale: Sections 2.3 and 4.2.1 cover evidenced household effects stolen in the forced entry, with no class sub-limit. Like-for-like high-street replacements are estimated at €850, excluding the coat and jacket billed separately.
Under §§6.2.1–6.2.2, brief seasonal use does not justify depreciation. The €289 purchase price is the best guide to like-for-like replacement.
Sections 7.1.8(c) and 7.1.9 exclude the upgrade premium, not the underlying loss. An equivalent mid-range waterproof jacket is estimated at €150.

Under §§4.2.2 and 6.3, the chain, earrings, bracelet and watch are valued at like-for-like replacement cost. The estimated €575 total is below the €3,000 event limit, and each piece is below the €1,000 item limit.
Sections 4.2.3 and 6.2.3 fix indemnity at the €6,500 agreed value, outside the unscheduled valuables limits. No deductible applies.

Sections 2.3.2(d) and 7.1.10 exclude the brooch because no supporting evidence is reported. The positive estimate is a rough conditional value if adequate evidence were supplied, subject to the €1,000 item limit.
Sections 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(e) expressly exclude personal travel to report the theft. The positive figure is a nominal estimate for a local round trip.
Sections 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(e) exclude the policyholder's claim preparation and reporting time. The positive figure is a nominal estimate for the time claimed.
Section 5.2.2 covers necessary overnight provisional securing, including call-out. An ordinary boarding charge of €290 is below the €1,000 gross event cap.
Sections 2.4.2 and 7.1.7 cover like-for-like replacement and fitting of the compromised lock and cylinder. The €230 estimate excludes any security upgrade or duplicate emergency attendance.
Sections 3.1.7 and 7.1.8(a) exclude cleaning superficial footprints even when billed by the locksmith. The positive figure is a nominal estimate for spot cleaning.
